messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — auth-service: unusual SSO token replay across ap-southeast-1 and eu-west-1. Error rate spike 5m rolling: 6.2% (baseline 0.02%). Possible token reuse or replay. Affected endpoints: /v1/session/refresh, /v1/auth/validate

alice_eng_oncall: paging. i'm on it. gathering logs now.

sam_sre: looking — i see repeated access with the same bearer token id across different source_ips. sample:
```
2026-03-15T02:12:09Z auth-service INFO token_id=abc123 user=svc-app src_ip=52.58.12.5 region=eu-west-1
2026-03-15T02:12:12Z auth-service INFO token_id=abc123 user=svc-app src_ip=13.250.89.2 region=ap-southeast-1
```
this suggests token replay, not normal session.

mariya_sec: thanks. any evidence of token exfil via logs or S3?

infra-engineer: customer reported finding logs in an S3 path that shouldn't be public: s3://redwood-staging-logs/2026/03/14/unauth/*. looks like staging bucket with debug logs containing auth headers.

ops-oncall: confirm — i can list the bucket. running:
```
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-staging-logs/2026/03/14/ --recursive | head
```
found file: s3://redwood-staging-logs/2026/03/14/debug-2026-03-14-23-11.log

alice_eng_oncall: that's bad. do we have PII or secrets in those logs? any Authorization headers?

infra-engineer: quick grep shows multiple lines with 'Authorization: Bearer'. e.g.
```
"Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...abc123..."
```

mariya_sec: immediate actions proposal:
- rotate any exposed client secrets/service tokens
- invalidate active sessions for affected client_id and user cohort
- apply ACL to S3 bucket (block public access) and audit access logs
- rotate KMS key used for token signing if necessary
- notify customers potentially impacted (CS + Legal to draft)

ops-oncall: doing S3 ACL now.

cs_representative: start drafting external customer notification template. who is impacted? we need a short blurb and remediation steps.

legal-ops: i'll review wording. we may need to notify customers if tokens were leaked. need list of affected accounts.

sam_sre: quick mitigation steps executed:
- revoked refresh tokens for client_id=svc-app (partial revocation to reduce blast radius)
- added temporary WAF rule to rate-limit suspicious src_ip ranges

alice_eng_oncall: running token invalidate job for token_id prefixes seen. command:
```
POST /internal/admin/invalidate_tokens
body: {"token_id_prefix":"abc"}
```

infra-engineer: S3 bucket ACL changed to private and block-public-access enabled. also enabled object lock audit for 90 days.

mariya_sec: on KMS rotation — we should not rotate signing key blindly without a rollout plan; instead create a new signing key, publish compatible signing key rotation, and set old key to expire after 24h. product-eng: can your clients handle key rollover?

product-eng: yes, SDKs honor key rotation header. we can push guidance in 2 hours.

ops-oncall: Ops note — we observed 1.2k token replays across both regions in last 3h. running regression to see earliest occurrence.

cs_representative: draft to customers:
"We detected unauthorized access to a staging logs bucket that contained session authorization headers for a small set of service integrations. We have revoked impacted tokens, secured the bucket, and are rotating credentials. No user plaintext PII has been identified so far. We'll follow up with steps to reconfigure any impacted service tokens."

legal-ops: good start. add line about internal investigation and contact info for security.

mariya_sec: next steps for triage:
1) enumerate affected token_ids and client_ids
2) escalate rotation for service tokens that appear in logs
3) check access logs to identify principals who downloaded the obj (iam principals)
4) decide customer notification scope with CS/legal

sam_sre: i can pull CloudTrail S3:GetObject events for s3://redwood-staging-logs/2026/03/14/ to get principals. starting query now.

alice_eng_oncall: notif to infra slack channel to pause any log export jobs that might be copying staging logs to third-party buckets.

infra-engineer: paused log-export cron for staging. added ephemeral flag to prevent accidental re-export.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigations applied: S3 ACL updated, temporary token revocation started, WAF rule enforced, log-export paused. Response owner: mariya_sec. Severity remains P1.

product-eng: ops, do we have a rollback plan if service tokens revocation causes outages for integrations?

ops-oncall: rollback path: reissue short-lived tokens and coordinate with partners. but current risk of not revoking is larger.

cs_representative: sending initial message to 4 affected customers now; will track responses in a follow-up thread.

legal-ops: open an incident ticket with classification 'Potential data exposure — auth headers in logs'. i'll attach required timeline template.

alice_eng_oncall: logging for post-incident: capture all commands run, timestamps, and the token invalidation list. i'll own the postmortem.

mariya_sec: handing off to night shift in 2h — @ops-oncall you'll be primary. please keep these mitigations in place and continue CloudTrail principal enumeration.

ops-oncall: acknowledged. will continue and file any new findings to the incident board. tagging #security for visibility.

incident-bot: :page_facing_up: Incident handed to ops-oncall at 2149998850. Please update the incident ticket when you change severity or customer communication.

alice_eng_oncall: flags for follow-up: audit why staging bucket was included in an export, tighten logging masks to strip Authorization headers by default (config change), and add a one-click token rotation tool for SSO clients.

mariya_sec: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene at 2149999200 for status update and plan next steps (postmortem + customer outreach cadence).
